extras.finding: issue: ir-design.md's new normative sentence and targetHint's lead claim an alias or variant takes its target node's hint, which is false for a $ref target under /paths. There positionHint declines and refHint falls back to the last token.
extras.why: Real at ebaa7d22. TestRefHint_Shapes' own row 'a pointer outside components falls back to its last token' wants 'items', while the declaration names the node response_item. No commit in this PR touches the sentence; even after ff688ad1, refHint yields schema_item. #553's merged version (5638dd62) scoped both ir-design.md and targetHint's doc with a /paths exception (#729).

extras.finding: issue: maxTargetHintHops' comment says reaching the cap means a document the cycle scan let through. In fact a legal 70-link acyclic chain of branch $refs compiles clean and falls back to positional names with no diagnostic.
extras.why: Reproduced at ebaa7d22: morphic compile -skip-validate on p4_chain70 exits 0 with no diagnostics. Its variant hints include 7 variant_0, where the 10-link control gives all 't'. #553's merged comment was rewritten to say an acyclic chain longer than the cap is legal and is named by where the walk stops. This PR's truth never touched it.

extras.finding: issue: guards with no reddening test: referencedBranch's branch check (M12), positionHint's components/schemas root checks (M16/M17), keyedSchemaMaps 'definitions'/'dependencies' (M5/M5b), and targetHint's name!="" guard (M11).
extras.why: Verified M5 at ebaa7d22: dropping "definitions" from keyedSchemaMaps leaves ./compilers/openapi/internal/schema and ./compilers/openapi green. #553's merged TestPositionHint_Shapes added rows for definitions/items, dependencies/items and /components/responses/..., which are the rows the review asked for. This PR's truth never added them.

extras.finding: issue: TestPureRefPosition_IsNamedByItsDeclarationInBothOrders credits the recorded hint ('The recorded hint fixes it') for rows positionHint already holds. Disabling the record leaves every row green. The /components/responses, /components/pathItems and shared-primitive shapes have no committed witness.
extras.why: The test doc overclaims what it pins. #553's merged doc was rewritten to 'Two things now hold each row, and either alone keeps it green... Only the second reaches under /paths'. This PR's truth never fixed it.

extras.finding: issue: TestSubSchemaHint_Fallbacks says neither fallback is reachable by a full compile, but both are (instrumented with p9_fallbacks). Also, subSchemaHint's `if ok { return hint }` after targetHint is redundant (an equivalent mutant).
extras.why: The redundant branch disappeared only incidentally, in ff688ad1's #529 rewrite of subSchemaHint. ff688ad1 kept the false 'Neither row a full compile reaches' claim. #553's merged version deleted the test. The review's reachability claim rests on its own instrumentation and was not rerun here, but the redundancy follows from the code.

extras.finding: question: a $ref to another union's inline branch is now hinted variant_N, which can duplicate a sibling's positional hint (p18: [variant_0, variant_0]).
extras.why: Posed as a design question. ir-design.md has no uniqueness rule for Variant.Name, and the parent build could already collide. No rule makes it a defect, and nothing in the truth or in #553 decided it.

extras.finding: nit: schema_test.go:2201 names structuralRole, a function this commit deleted (it became the structuralRoles map).
extras.why: Confirmed at ebaa7d22: `git grep structuralRole\b` hits only that comment line. The stale reference is gone in #553's merged version.

extras.finding: nit: TestRefHint_Shapes cites #520 for percent-decoding a non-pointer reference, but #520 is about pointer fragments.
extras.why: #520 concerns a percent-encoded non-UTF-8 byte in a $ref fragment reaching an IR identifier. The cited UTF-8 check on percent-decoding guards exactly that. main still cites #520 at the same non-pointer decoding site (compose.go:1104, 'a reference whose fragment spells no pointer ... not UTF-8 (GitHub #520)'), and #553 kept the cite.

extras.finding: nit: test comments say 'On main these read ...' and 'the order that was wrong on main', which go false once merged.
extras.why: Once merged, 'main' refers to this code, so the comments become false. #553's merged schema_test.go no longer carries them. This is a low-severity wording defect, but a real one.

missed_patterns: None of this PR's later commits fix a defect introduced by the initial commit. They are stacked continuation (#529, #530), fixes to later commits, or a pre-existing crash, so recall here is not measurable. The one adjacent gap: the review endorsed positionHint's claim that 'only the reference reaches' unwalked positions without probing two references at different depths into such a region under /paths. It also never probed reference-before-declaration where the target's body refers back above it, which reaches a node still being built (#749, a panic on the parent and on the initial commit alike). Instruction change: when a change touches reference-driven interning or naming, probe (a) two references at different depths into a region no declaration lowers, under both /components and /paths, and (b) a reference lowered before its declaration whose target refers back to an ancestor. Report such pre-existing failures under Pre-existing.
